_about: A crash on a highway in or next to our district, heard first on another agency's channel (sizeup/intel/highway.py, engine.py step 6 for a "highway": true category). Scope: every captured channel with words (police, EMS, fire, DOT, interop, transit; the context talkgroups included) except the police pack's own (they push their own crashes) and our own dispatch channel. One category, crash: held at log until the words put it on a highway segment within highway.buffer_m of our district (an exit, a mile marker, or two routes and a ramp word: the gazetteer's markers), or name the route alone on a source whose own town has that route by our district. One event per crash across sources (same route, within highway.merge_m), later transmissions attach; our own call at it (the county's dispatch, within highway.link_min after) links it and stops its pushes. While a crash event is live, its source is transcribed like ours for highway.promote_min (the operating-channel promotion, sizeup/cad/opchannel.py). Its sources are not made push sources for speech-to-text ("stt_high": false): Settings can turn that on. An injury, EMS or an agency word is a cue only (beside a crash word), never a crash alone; cleared, reopened, gone on arrival or no injuries is none (or damps it). The local model (sizeup/intel/backing.py) is asked only about rows with a highway word (\"model_needs\"), at most model_hour_cap an hour of its own, and what it raises alone stays on the map (\"model_mode\": \"map\"): never a push without a rule. Generic phrases only, in data/intel/tables/stt.json's spelling ("rollover", "guardrail", number words as digits). A count of cars alone is weak: police say "two cars" for patrol cars; "N car" said with a crash word, a highway word or a route is a crash.
